{{Nihongo|'''Hironari Miyazawa'''|宮沢 弘成|Miyazawa Hironari|1927–2023}} was a Japanese [[particle physics|particle]] and [[nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]], known for his work in [[supersymmetry]], which was first proposed by Miyazawa in 1966 as a possible [[Symmetry (physics)|symmetry]] between [[meson]]s and [[baryon]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal | author=H. Miyazawa| date=1966| title=Baryon Number Changing Currents| journal=Prog. Theor. Phys.| volume=36| issue=6| pages=1266–1276| doi=10.1143/PTP.36.1266| bibcode=1966PThPh..36.1266M| doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | author=H. Miyazawa| date=1968| title=Spinor Currents and Symmetries of Baryons and Mesons| journal=Phys. Rev.| volume=170| issue=5| pages=1586–1590| doi=10.1103/PhysRev.170.1586| bibcode=1968PhRv..170.1586M}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book | author=P. G. O. Freund |author-link=Peter Freund| date=1988| title=Introduction to Supersymmetry (Cambridge Monographs on Mathematical Physics)| publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]| isbn=978-0-521-35675-6}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | author = S. Catto |date = 2008 |url = http://nucl.phys.s.u-tokyo.ac.jp/kimiko/fm50/catto.pdf |title = Miyazawa Supersymmetry |journal = AIP Conf. Proc. |volume = 1011 |issue = 1 |pages = 253–258 |doi = 10.1063/1.2932297
|bibcode = 2008AIPC.1011..253C}}{{dead link|date=November 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Miyazawa studied physics and received his undergraduate degree in 1950 at the [[University of Tokyo]]. He joined the faculty after he received his doctorate in 1953 from the University of Tokyo, and became a full professor of physics in 1968. In 1988 he moved to the [[Kanagawa University]] and served there until 1998. He was a professor emeritus of the University of Tokyo. During these periods, he also served visiting professorships at the [[University of Chicago]] and the [[University of Minnesota]], and directorship at the Meson Science Laboratory, the University of Tokyo.

From 1953 to 1955 he was a research associate at the [[Enrico Fermi Institute|Institute for Nuclear Studies]], the University of Chicago, where he conducted research on theoretical
nuclear physics under [[Gregor Wentzel]] and [[Enrico Fermi]].<ref>{{Cite journal | author = H. Miyazawa |date = 2010 |title = Superalgebra and fermion-boson symmetry |journal = Proc. Jpn. Acad. Ser. B |volume = 86 |issue = 3 |pages = 158–164 |doi = 10.2183/pjab.86.158 |pmid = 20228617 |bibcode = 2010PJAB...86..158M|pmc = 3417842}}</ref> A [[supersymmetry]] relating [[mesons]] and [[baryon]]s was first proposed, in the context of hadronic physics, by Miyazawa in 1966. This supersymmetry did not involve spacetime, that is, it concerned internal symmetry, and was broken badly. Miyazawa's work was largely ignored at the time.<ref>{{Cite journal | author=H. Miyazawa| year=1966| title=Baryon Number Changing Currents| journal=Prog. Theor. Phys.| volume=36| pages=1266–1276| doi=10.1143/PTP.36.1266| issue=6| bibcode = 1966PThPh..36.1266M |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | author=H. Miyazawa | year=1968| title=Spinor Currents and Symmetries of Baryons and Mesons| journal=Phys. Rev.| volume=170| issue=5| pages=1586–1590| doi=10.1103/PhysRev.170.1586| bibcode = 1968PhRv..170.1586M }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last=Kaku |first=Michio |author-link=Michio Kaku |title=Quantum Field Theory |isbn=0-19-509158-2 |page=663|year=1993 |publisher=Oxford University Press }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last=Freund |first=Peter |author-link=Peter Freund |title=Introduction to Supersymmetry |isbn=0-521-35675-X |pages=26–27, 138|date=1988-03-31 |publisher=Cambridge University Press }}</ref>

Hironari Miyazawa died in 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Rigakubu News, March 2023 |url=https://dl5s7ayfvssw3.cloudfront.net/WEB_info/p/pub/9301/2023年3月号（54巻6号）_提出用（通常用）.pdf |website=School of Science, The University Of Tokyo |access-date=14 October 2023}}</ref>
